1: You are the dragon today. Not the knight, not the princess. Put on the scales and wait to be addressed as Great.
2: Be the mare, and don't steer. Become the weather the carriage is driving into. Pack a bag for the south-west and a eulogy for the north-east.
3: The seed is stuck and has opinions. Do not go out in the rain to help it. Appoint a small committee of moss.
4: A young person knocks. Answer once, in full. A second knock gets a pamphlet; a third gets the cat.
5: Wait at the bank with your shoes on your head. The river has been told you're coming. Cross when it nods.
6: You are right, and it isn't helping. Drop the argument like a wet umbrella in the hall and go and see someone enormous. Do not cross anything.
7: Raise a small army. It needs a leader who has done this before and a snack tent. No one is to be called troops.
8: Press yourself against the people who press back. First check your pockets for stones. Whoever arrives last gets the cold soup.
9: The clouds have gathered and nothing has been said. Wear the raincoat anyway. Carry an umbrella indoors as a statement.
10: You stepped on the tiger's tail and it only looked at you. Apologise in your most beautiful voice and keep walking.
11: Small things are leaving and big things are arriving, neither with luggage. Hold the door. Do not ask which is which.
12: Heaven and earth have stopped speaking, and you are in the room between them. Take no side. Read a magazine very loudly.
13: Gather in a field with people you didn't pick. Leave the rooms with locks. Bring something heavy to carry across a stream together.
14: You own the sun, for now. It was a clerical error. Enjoy it, and tell no one the paperwork is wrong.
15: Hide under your own greatness like a cat under a towel. It works, and everyone will see that it works.
16: Everyone has started dancing and no one knows who began it. Go along with it. March with sparkling intent.
17: Follow something that doesn't know it is leading: a parade, a pigeon. Keep a respectful distance and your name out of it.
18: Something in the cupboard has become a new life form. Clean it out over three days, and name it first.
19: Great things approach on small feet. By the eighth month there will be trouble. Mark it on the calendar in red and wear something unwise.
20: Hands washed, offering still in your pocket. Stand in the doorway until the room wonders what you're carrying. Let them guess, then be magnificent about it.
21: Something is lodged between your teeth and it is the truth. Bite, don't floss. Wear the consequences as jewellery.
22: Decorate, but not the whole house and not the dog. The ornament should know it's a guest.
23: It's all coming off, like wallpaper, like a wig in a gale. Don't paste. Stand under the falling and see what you look like with nothing on the walls.
24: Come back after seven days like a lost glove with a new personality. The door was never locked. Bring friends or don't.
25: Behave in a full room exactly as you would in an empty one. Anything else is a rumour you started about yourself.
26: Stop living off the family cheese. Go out and feed yourself, loudly, in public. The great stream is waiting, and so is someone's boat.
27: Feed the mouth you've been ashamed of. Look at the menu: you may want to replace dinner with a poem.
28: The ridge-pole is bending like a rude bow. Don't prop it. Leave the house in any direction at all, preferably with a flourish.
29: Fall in. Bring a snack. The abyss has waited ages for good company and will teach you the sea by being extremely rude.
30: Be fire with the temperament of a cow. Burn very slowly, in the direction of the grass.
31: Touch what attracts you as lightly as a moth that has read the instructions. Any wedding should be conducted by the moth.
32: Do the same strange thing for a very long time and call it a lifestyle. Move in any direction, but move steadily.
33: Leave the party at its height, like a legend, like fog. Small stubborn things stay. Take your coat.
34: You are enormous and also correct. Proceed carefully, like a piano being moved up a flight of stairs.
35: You've been given a great many horses and seen three times in one day. Accept the horses. Learn their names.
36: The sun has gone into the wardrobe. Sit in the dark and glitter anyway; sequins bring their own light.
37: The household runs on whoever holds it together. Find out who that is and give them a hat.
38: Two people turn their backs and still point at the same moon. Small matters will go well. Do not hold a summit.
39: The road is a lame goat. Go south-west, away from the thing you keep calling north-east. Find an elder with a good umbrella.
40: The knot gives. If nothing is left to do, go home and lie on the floor. If something is, do it before lunch.
41: Take away until two bowls of rice are a feast. Offer them to someone as if they were the whole sea.
42: Everything you touch gets a bit more, so touch recklessly. Cross the water. Take the long way round just to look.
43: Name the offender in the town square, then quietly in your own kitchen. Don't start a war. Start with a very loud letter.
44: A creature walks in that has never once been furniture. Don't wed it. Offer soup, a door, and your phone number, and see what it takes.
45: Gather at the family shrine and meet the very tall person. Bring a real offering, preferably a goat that is fond of you. Everything is allowed.
46: Grow like a tree that has been told a secret. Go up, slowly, towards the south. The great person will be there, putting away their umbrella.
47: You are in a dry well with an opinion. Speak less. Words aren't currency down here; try bartering with a hat.
48: Towns move and the well stays. Draw from it, and do not break the bucket on the last inch.
49: Nothing is true until the glitter lands, and then everyone will say they always knew. Let them. Change your name in the mirror first.
50: The cauldron is the size of a small cathedral and bubbling. Great success. Don't look in; hand out spoons.
51: Thunder arrives and a hundred miles of people drop things. You, with a ladle in your hand, keep stirring.
52: Sit like a mountain and lose your back. Walk in the yard and see no one; no one sees you either. Fine.
53: The goose arrives in stages: a rock, a tree, a roof. Do this. Arrive at the marriage in stages, with luggage.
54: Any move is a mistake today, like wearing a veil in a swimming pool. Do it anyway only if it makes a good story.
55: Be the sun at noon: no shadows, no apologies, no notes. Don't worry about the afternoon. It has its own job.
56: Travel light and be polite to strangers. A small success will be waiting in a doorway. Carry only what can be sung.
57: Be the draught under a door. Go in any direction and make small differences. Visit the elder, who will pretend not to notice you.
58: Talk and laugh with your whole face. It is correct. Don't let anyone tidy it.
59: Scatter like dandelion fluff at the temple. Cross the water as a rumour. Be correct about something small.
60: A rule that hurts to follow isn't a rule, it's a hat that's too small. Unpick it and make something wearable.
61: Be so sincere that pigs and fish are moved. Test it on the nearest pig. Cross the water with a full heart and a cold sandwich.
62: Do small things loudly and don't attempt the big thing. A bird's song falls, it doesn't rise. Be a bird who has accepted gravity.
63: You finished, and now there is chaos in the pantry. This is the usual order. Stay steady and keep one eye on the ending.
64: The fox gets her tail wet at the very last step, and so do you. Good: a dry tail is a lie. Be the soggy hero.
